paper.authors_full: Chenghai Liu, Jiayao Guo, Rongxia Gao, Xiangnan Chen, Qiuhan Zhu, Pengcheng Chang
paper.title: Borrowed or kept? How self-generation-first and direct-adoption AI workflows shape immediate unaided reasoning
paper.pdf_filename: Liu et al (2026) - Borrowed or kept.pdf
paper.version_read: Published journal article, Frontiers in Psychology 17:1910545, published 14 September 2026; DOI 10.3389/fpsyg.2026.1910545 (PDF p. 1).
paper.one_line_finding: On the unaided essay 15-20 minutes later, direct-adoption AI reduced reasoning quality (-0.38, d = -0.28) and within-essay flexibility (-0.30, d = -0.23) versus No-AI, but not originality (q = 0.28); self-generation-first did not fall below No-AI (pp. 7-8, Section 3.4).
paper.shared_samples: No overlap reported. The document explicitly states that the present sample is independent of both DACOS development samples in Zhu et al. (2026), Not all cognitive offloading is equal: distinguishing dependent and autonomous offloading to generative AI.

studies.label: Three-arm workflow experiment (argumentative essay with or without AI, then unaided parallel essay)

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 1, abstract (study totals); PDF p. 4, Table 2, Randomized and Primary analysis sample rows (columns Autonomous, Dependent, No-AI).

arms.name: Autonomous
arms.description: Self-generation-first AI workflow: draft a thesis and outline before the AI panel unlocks, compare and question the AI points, then rewrite in own words. The later essay is unaided (PDF p. 5, Sections 2.4-2.5).

arms.name: Dependent
arms.description: Direct-adoption AI workflow: generate arguments and paragraphs with AI and adopt the output with minimal changes, without a required initial outline. The later essay is unaided (PDF p. 5, Sections 2.4-2.5).

arms.name: No-AI
arms.description: Write independently with AI tools, search engines, and external materials prohibited; the later essay is also unaided (PDF p. 5, Sections 2.4-2.5).

studies.task: Write argumentative policy essays about city-center car bans and a shorter work week, first under the assigned AI or No-AI workflow and then without AI in the same session, with topic placement counterbalanced (PDF p. 3, Section 2.1; PDF p. 5, Sections 2.3-2.5).

ai_tool.name: Qwen3.5 (Tongyi Qianwen; Alibaba Cloud)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 5, Section 2.5. Served through the study platform using its official API; the model release year and exact pinned version identifier are not printed.

preregistration.where: PDF p. 3, Section 2.1.1: "The study was not formally preregistered". A dated internal analysis plan preceded analysis; it is not a formal preregistration.

not_extracted.what: S1-O1: Phase-2 unaided reasoning quality; Dependent versus No-AI, Autonomous versus No-AI, and Autonomous versus Dependent; all reported ANCOVA sensitivity specifications
not_extracted.reason: Excluded by extraction-spec rule 6 and codebook Sections 1 and 6 as argumentative-writing proficiency. The same rubric defines baseline writing ability (PDF p. 5, Section 2.3; PDF p. 6, Section 2.8), and assesses thesis clarity, evidence, reasoning coherence, and counterarguments rather than the creativity or usefulness of an idea. PDF p. 6, Section 2.6: "Reasoning quality captured the clarity of the thesis, the relevance and suﬃciency of evidence, the coherence of the reasoning, and the handling of counterarguments;" This reconciliation supersedes the screening form's usefulness classification; the proficiency exclusion is not limited to IELTS or language-mechanics composites. Excluded by extraction-spec rule 5 because the reported effect adjusts for time measured after assignment. PDF p. 6, Section 2.8: "For Phase-2 (transfer) models, the covariates were baseline writing ability and Phase-2 time on task, and for Phase-1 models, baseline ability and Phase-1 time." PDF p. 4, Table 1 note: "the two time-on-task rows are post-treatment and are reported as descriptive evidence about what the manipulation changed, not as balance checks." The main contrasts are in PDF pp. 7-8, Section 3.4 and Figure 2. This exclusion also covers per-protocol, HC3, individual-rater, additional time/effort/performance adjustments, relaxed exclusions, available-case and multiple-imputation analyses, missing-outcome scenarios, AI-screen reinstatement, and analyst-set threshold checks (PDF p. 9, Sections 3.5-3.7; PDF p. 10, Table 4). The Table 4 note states: "All models are ANCOVAs adjusting for baseline writing ability and Phase-2 time on task unless the speciﬁcation states otherwise; p-values are two-sided and uncorrected."

not_extracted.what: S1-O2: Phase-2 unaided idea diversity; Dependent versus No-AI, Autonomous versus No-AI, and Autonomous versus Dependent; additional Phase-1-duration adjustment
not_extracted.reason: Excluded by extraction-spec rule 5 because the reported effect adjusts for time measured after assignment. PDF p. 6, Section 2.8: "For Phase-2 (transfer) models, the covariates were baseline writing ability and Phase-2 time on task, and for Phase-1 models, baseline ability and Phase-1 time." PDF p. 4, Table 1 note: "the two time-on-task rows are post-treatment and are reported as descriptive evidence about what the manipulation changed, not as balance checks." The outcome is within-essay flexibility, not diversity across people (PDF p. 6, Section 2.6). All reported main contrasts and arm means are adjusted (PDF p. 8, Section 3.4 and Figure 2); the additional Phase-1-duration model also conditions on a post-treatment variable (PDF p. 9, Section 3.5). No unadjusted or baseline-only adjusted result is printed. Figure-only values were not estimated.

not_extracted.what: S1-O1: Baseline-to-Phase-2 reasoning-quality change means; Dependent versus No-AI, Autonomous versus No-AI, and Autonomous versus Dependent (s1_reasoning_change_dependent_vs_no_ai, s1_reasoning_change_autonomous_vs_no_ai, s1_reasoning_change_autonomous_vs_dependent)
not_extracted.reason: Excluded by extraction-spec rule 6 and codebook Sections 1 and 6 as argumentative-writing proficiency. The same rubric defines baseline writing ability (PDF p. 5, Section 2.3; PDF p. 6, Section 2.8), and assesses thesis clarity, evidence, reasoning coherence, and counterarguments rather than the creativity or usefulness of an idea. PDF p. 6, Section 2.6: "Reasoning quality captured the clarity of the thesis, the relevance and suﬃciency of evidence, the coherence of the reasoning, and the handling of counterarguments;" This reconciliation supersedes the screening form's usefulness classification; the proficiency exclusion is not limited to IELTS or language-mechanics composites. PDF p. 12, Section 4.5 reports: "the no-AI arm was essentially unchanged (−0.02 on the 1–7 scale), the autonomous arm gained slightly (+0.17), and the dependent arm lost substantially (−0.49;" These are changes on the same reasoning-quality rubric. B transcribed the arm changes correctly, but they remain outside outcome scope. The change-score paragraph does not state covariate adjustment, so this exclusion does not assume that it inherits the ANCOVA time covariate. Only an omnibus between-arm test accompanies the means; no pairwise difference, pairwise uncertainty, SD, or analysis-specific participant count is printed. None is derived from the means or degrees of freedom.

open_items: The paper prints no unadjusted or baseline-only adjusted arm contrasts, raw arm means, or participant-level outcome SDs for originality or within-essay idea diversity in either phase. These are the missing statistics needed for eligible creativity estimates without conditioning on post-treatment time (PDF p. 6, Section 2.8; PDF pp. 7-8, Sections 3.2-3.4).

Figure 2 supplies adjusted arm means and uncertainty graphically; no values were read from the plots. The complete PDF identifies no appendix or separate supplement with raw outcome statistics. Full instructions, the rubric, model configuration, de-identified data, and analysis materials are offered only on request and were not supplied (PDF p. 5, Section 2.5; PDF p. 8, Figure 2; PDF p. 13, Data availability statement).

Participant residence country is not stated. The paper describes Chinese-speaking students and early-career workers recruited online; country remains null (PDF p. 3, Section 2.2; PDF p. 13, Section 4.5).
Raters were trained and blind, but their professional credentials are not stated (PDF p. 6, Section 2.6).
The Qwen3.5 release year, pinned model identifier, and sampling-parameter values are not printed. Model year remains null rather than being inferred from the publication year (PDF p. 5, Section 2.5).

The power paragraph gives achieved cells of 209–225, inconsistent with the explicitly printed primary arm counts of 222, 225, and 212. Study counts follow the participant section and flow table; the origin of the power-paragraph discrepancy remains unknown (PDF p. 3, Section 2.2; PDF p. 4, Table 2; PDF pp. 6-7, Section 2.8).
